Herodian’s -ιξ / -ιγξ / -υξ Accent Toy

Play with endings like Θρῇξ, σάλπιγξ, κῆρυξ. Type a Greek word; the gadget guesses its “accent tendency” (very roughly) and lets you try synaloepha-style contraction like Θρέϊξ → Θρῇξ.

1) Try a word

What is this showing?

Herodian lists many words ending in -ιξ, -ιγξ, -υξ and comments on accent/prosody. One rule here: τὰ εἰς -υξ βαρύνεται (“words in -υξ are barytone”), unless they have an “inclusive” meaning.

This toy does heuristics: it detects endings and gives a playful accent suggestion (not a full accentuation engine). It also demonstrates synaloepha like Θρέϊξ → Θρῇξ by contracting ϊ/ΐ + vowel sequences.

One ending, different accents

Words in -ψος with more than two syllables: final acute.

Neuter nouns in -ος: barytone, with the accent before the final syllable.
τετυφός · πεποιηκός
Neuter participles: final acute, like their masculine forms.
φιλάνθρωπος · Ἑλλήσποντος
Listed compound examples: accent on the third syllable from the end.

Here βαρύνεται means barytone (non-final accent); it does not tell us to print a grave accent. Grammar and syllable count matter. Listed compounds illustrate the passage; this tool does not infer a compound rule for unfamiliar words.

Herodian’s -ιξ / -ιγξ / -υξ Accent Toy

Play with endings like Θρῇξ, σάλπιγξ, κῆρυξ. Type a Greek word; the gadget guesses its “accent tendency” (very roughly) and lets you try synaloepha-style contraction like Θρέϊξ → Θρῇξ.

What is this showing?

Herodian lists many words ending in -ιξ, -ιγξ, -υξ and comments on accent/prosody. One rule here: τὰ εἰς -υξ βαρύνεται (“words in -υξ are barytone”), unless they have an “inclusive” meaning.

This toy does heuristics: it detects endings and gives a playful accent suggestion (not a full accentuation engine). It also demonstrates synaloepha like Θρέϊξ → Θρῇξ only for the two attested inputs Θρέϊξ / Θρῆϊξ. Other forms are preserved. Inclusive meaning cannot be inferred from spelling; supply it yourself if known.
